html:
A multi-sport event held every two years among the countries of Southeast Asia. It began as the South East Asian Peninsular Games in Bangkok in December 1959 and is now one of the region's biggest shared events.

The idea came from Thailand's Olympic committee, which wanted smaller countries to get more top level competition than the Asian Games offered. The first games brought together athletes from Thailand, Burma, Malaya, Singapore, South Vietnam and Laos. In 1977 Indonesia and the Philippines joined and the name became the Southeast Asian Games. Today all eleven countries of the region take part.

The games grew alongside regional cooperation such as the founding of ASEAN in 1967, and they let neighbours who had fought wars meet in sport. Hosts may add local sports such as sepak takraw, a kick volleyball game, and the traditional martial arts of the region, along with Olympic events. See Thailand and the earlier Melbourne Olympics of 1956, the first held in the southern hemisphere.
sum: A multi-sport event held every two years among the countries of Southeast Asia. It began as the South East Asian Peninsular Games in Bangkok in December 1959 and is now one of the region's biggest shared events.
